title: Debunking Alarmist Narratives on the ‘China Air Base’ in Laos
gist: Olli Pekka Suorsa argues that the newly opened China-backed Laos-China Joint Support and Training Center and Friendship Aviation Academy at Ban Keun, Laos is being overhyped by China hawks and media as Beijing's third overseas military base and first Southeast Asian air base.

insights.claim: The Laos-China Joint Support and Training Center and the Friendship Aviation Academy at Ban Keun, Vientiane province, Laos opened on September 29, 2026, triggering an intense media storm.
insights.speaker: Olli Pekka Suorsa
insights.so_what: A new China-linked military-adjacent facility in mainland Southeast Asia is a regional security headline risk.
insights.quote: The opening of the Laos-China Joint Support and Training Center and the Friendship Aviation Academy in Ban Keun, Laos on September 29 has sparked an intense media storm.

insights.claim: China hawks claim the China-backed Ban Keun airfield in Laos is Beijing's third overseas military base after Djibouti and Ream in Cambodia, and its first air base in Southeast Asia.
insights.speaker: Olli Pekka Suorsa
insights.so_what: Shows how the PLA overseas-basing narrative is expanding, shaping Western threat perceptions in the region.
insights.quote: China hawks claim that the innocuous airfield represents Beijing’s third overseas military base

insights.claim: The author contends that the Ban Keun airfield in Laos is innocuous and that labelling it a Chinese 'air base' with 'attack aircraft' is alarmist mischaracterization of training aircraft.
insights.speaker: Olli Pekka Suorsa
insights.so_what: Argues the market/policy reaction to Chinese basing headlines in Southeast Asia may be overstated.

insights.claim: Alarmists warn China could lengthen the Ban Keun runway and expand infrastructure to project power across mainland Southeast Asia, collect intelligence, support bomber operations, or outflank Vietnam.
insights.speaker: Olli Pekka Suorsa
insights.so_what: Identifies the escalation scenarios that would make the facility strategically material, especially for Vietnam.
insights.quote: Still others have proposed that an enlarged base could facilitate bomber operations or to out-flank or surround Vietnam.
